name: Viakable
subsector: power and building wire and cable
desc: Mexican maker of electrical conductors, magnet wire and power cable, founded 1956 as Conductores Monterrey, with plants in Mexico and the US.
products: Building wire, medium/high-voltage cable, magnet wire (Viakon, Magnekon, CME, Multipak reels, Vialutek)
customers: Utilities, construction, industry, distributors; projects named: Auditorio Nacional, La Venta II wind farm, Paseo de la Reforma
marketing_autonomy_basis: Own brand portfolio, own website, own director general (Carlos Ramos Espinosa per xignux.com/nuestro-holding) and own rebrand in Feb 2026
stores_or_sites: Plants in Mexico (Monterrey area, San Luis Potosí, Querétaro, Durango) and US (CME Wire & Cable)
markets: Mexico and United States/Canada (CME Wire & Cable), sales representatives and distributors in Central America, South America and the Caribbean

signals.what: 'Evolucionamos nuestra identidad': brand identity evolution announced

fit_rationale: Largest Mexican-owned power-cable maker (USD 3bn revenue) selling into US utilities and data-centre/construction markets; Mexico City and US races give B2B hospitality for utility and contractor buyers.
f1_markets: Mexico, United States (Miami, Austin, Las Vegas), Canada

access.roles: Director General Viakable; Xignux Director de Desarrollo Corporativo

outstanding: Parent Xignux is on the master as 'Xignux S.A. de C.V.': confirm the user accepts the subsidiary separately. Employee count not stated for Viakable alone (Xignux group 23,000).

name: INTERprotección
desc: Mexican insurance, surety, reinsurance and microinsurance broker that describes itself as Latin America's largest, with the digital broker inter.mx.
products: Corporate insurance and surety broking, reinsurance broking, microinsurance, assistance services, inter.mx digital broker
customers: Mexican companies of all sizes; consumers via inter.mx
markets: Mexico; operates in 150+ countries through alliances with Macquarie and Gallagher

fin.note: Expansión 500 (2026 edition) rank 127; Expansión marks the figure "e" (its own estimate); the figure likely reflects premiums placed rather than broker commission revenue

fit_rationale: Corporate insurance broker whose business is relationships with Mexican CFOs and risk managers; already buys premium tennis sponsorships for hospitality, so a Mexico City GP or team deal fits its pattern.
category_conflict: potential: insurance/broking partners exist on several F1 teams
outstanding: Revenue figure is an Expansión estimate that probably counts premiums intermediated; commission revenue not published. Ownership: site says 100% Mexican; owners not named on pages opened. No dated news page found.
